Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a new function, read the existing module and its helpers (e.g. money utilities like to_money/round_money/ZERO) and reuse them so rounding and type conventions stay consistent with the rest of the codebase.
[ace-0002] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Run the full test suite after implementing to confirm nothing regressed, and check for a task-specific test file (e.g. tests/test_<function>.py) that pins expected behavior.
[ace-0004] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Mirror the error-handling conventions of sibling modules: reuse the same exception class and error codes (e.g. BillingError with codes like "invalid_state") and copy the exact message format used elsewhere (e.g. f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}") so behavior stays consistent.
[ace-0006] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: After implementing, exercise edge cases manually (zero/negative/float/bool quantity, negative price, NaN, wrong invoice status) in addition to running the test suite, to confirm each validation path raises the expected error code.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When computing a weighted average, guard against division by zero (empty lines / zero total quantity) and return the domain's zero constant rather than raising or returning a float.
[ace-0005] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) since True/False are ints in Python, and reject non-int types like floats before comparing, so invalid input raises the domain error rather than slipping through.

item.content: When a function must return the first occurrence strictly after a given time, compute the index with floor division plus one: n = (after - start) // length + 1, and handle the before-start case separately (return start + length) so the start itself is never returned as a renewal.

Reuse the module's datetime normalization helper (e.g. ensure_utc) on both the query time and the stored start time before doing arithmetic, so naive/aware mismatches and non-datetime inputs raise the domain error consistently.

In ledgerly, Subscription has fields period_days (int) and started_at (datetime); sibling module subscriptions.current_period shows the canonical pattern of ensure_utc + timedelta(days=period_days) + floor division for period math, and BillingError(code, message) is the shared error type.
